$comment: THE ONE DEPENDENCY FLOOR, as data. THIS FILE IS THE CANONICAL COPY.
Every repo in the shared-element programme — vrtc-pipeline, gst_vtpl_src, and
the five library repos — builds against these exact versions.
WHY A FILE AND NOT A CONVENTION. vcpkg honours 'builtin-baseline' and
'overrides' ONLY in the top-level manifest; a port's own overrides are
ignored. So the floor cannot be INHERITED by the consumers — it has to be
restated in each one's vcpkg.json and kept in step by a check rather than by
mechanism. This file is what those checks compare against.
WHY IT LIVES INSIDE A PORT. The plan (T-20) called for a canonical copy in the
registry plus a metadata-only port mirroring it 'for discoverability'. That is
two copies of the thing whose entire purpose is to be the only copy, so they
are collapsed: the port directory IS the canonical location, and portfile.cmake
installs this file rather than fetching it. Consumers therefore read it OFFLINE
from vcpkg_installed/<triplet>/share/vtpl-dependency-floor/ after resolution,
with no network in the check and no vendored duplicate to drift. Editing the
floor is a version bump of this port, which is correct: consumers pin it.
WHY THESE VERSIONS. Not because they are newest, but because they are the
only set already proven on the predecessor's entire effective target set:
Ubuntu 22.04 (DS 7.0), Ubuntu 24.04 (DS 8.0), Intel DL Streamer, the SDK-free
CPU image, and Windows MSVC. gst_vtpl_src pins grpc 1.51.1 / protobuf 3.21.12
/ abseil 20230802.1 against a 2023 baseline, and moving vrtc-pipeline down to
meet it would sacrifice the Windows port and two years of transitive security
fixes. It also erases a real portability defect: vtpl_grpc_args.h includes
<grpc/impl/channel_arg_names.h>, which did not exist before gRPC ~1.57.
PROVENANCE. A vcpkg checkout provisioned from scratch at VCPKG_REF resolved
grpc 1.76.0#1 / openssl 3.6.2 / protobuf 6.33.4#2 / abseil 20260107.1#3 —
this floor exactly. Measured 2026-08-26 on a Windows box, so the numbers
below are an observation and not an aspiration.
A TAG, deliberately: the dev images clone with `git clone --branch $VCPKG_REF`,
so an untagged commit would force them all to clone-then-checkout for nothing.
The two overridden ports did not move at all - grpc and openssl are pinned by
'overrides' and resolve identically either side. The two resolved-only ports
moved by PORT-VERSION only, protobuf 6.33.4#1 -> #2 and abseil 20260107.1#2 ->
#3: vcpkg packaging revisions of the same upstream releases, which is the
cheapest shape a floor move can have. Both were measured before the bump, not
discovered after it - which is what the resolved-only entries are FOR.
MOVING THE FLOOR is a programme-level decision, not a repo-level one: bump it
here, bump this port's version, then update every consumer, in one change. The
predecessor additionally cannot move until the five prebuilt binaries in its
thirdparty/ that carry gRPC/protobuf/abseil symbols are rebuilt — the plan's
T-22. That work is the real gate, and it lives outside both repos.
THE WINDOWS TRIPLET IS HERE TOO, and for the same reason as the versions: it
is a pin vcpkg will not let a port hand down, so every consumer restates it
and only a check keeps them in step. It had already been copied by hand once.
vcpkg reads a triplet at RESOLVE time, before any port is installed, so this
port cannot ship the .cmake file usefully — it ships the SETTINGS as data and
each repo's triplet file is checked against them.

$notes.override: Restated in each consumer's vcpkg.json 'overrides' block, because vcpkg ignores a port's own overrides.
$notes.resolved-only: Not pinned by an override — it follows from the baseline plus grpc's dependency graph. Recorded so a baseline bump that silently moves protobuf or abseil is visible as drift rather than as a surprise at link time on Windows.
$notes.consumers: Read the INSTALLED copy at share/vtpl-dependency-floor/dependency-floor.json in your vcpkg_installed tree, not a vendored one. A repo that cannot yet depend on this port (because taking the private registry as a dependency would break credential-less builds) may hold a mirror, but must check it against this file — vrtc-pipeline's scripts/check_floor_mirror.sh is that check.
$notes.windows_triplet: Settled 2026-08-25 (plan T-14 / decision 6), against gst_vtpl_src's x64-mixed. NOT a preference: x64-mixed is static-by-default with nine dynamic exceptions, and protobuf is not among them, so protobuf links STATICALLY there — which gives each module its own descriptor pool and makes a duplicate descriptor table SILENT. Under x64-windows-vrtc protobuf is shared (measured: libprotobuf.dll and abseil_dll.dll in the WIN-0 deploy inventory, and no gRPC DLL at all), so there is one pool per process and a duplicate registration aborts with 'File already exists in database'. That is precisely the failure the programme's WIN-1 gate exists to catch, so x64-mixed would make the gate pass vacuously. The static-OpenSSL clause is separately load-bearing: GStreamer ships its own libcrypto-3-x64.dll / libssl-3-x64.dll under the filenames vcpkg builds, and Windows resolves DLLs by name process-wide. COST, recorded honestly: gst_vtpl_src's Windows build (JenkinsfileAll, not the matrix Jenkinsfile, which excludes every Windows combination) must move, flipping poco, opencv and the rest from static to dynamic. Fold that into the manifest re-resolve the floor bump already forces.
